questions.stem: The Vijayanagar empire was founded in the year:
questions.explanation: Founded by brothers Harihara I and Bukka I in 1336 on the south bank of Tungabhadra, with the blessings of their guru Vidyaranya. Capital Hampi — ruins are a UNESCO WHS. Lasted till 1646.
questions.subject: History

questions.explanation: Krishnadeva Raya — greatest Vijayanagar emperor. Defeated Orissa's Gajapatis, Sultans of Bijapur and Golconda. Patron of Telugu literature — 'Amuktamalyada' (Telugu poem) and Sanskrit 'Jambavati Kalyanam'. The 'Ashtadiggaja' — 8 Telugu poets at his court (notably Allasani Peddana). r. 1509-1529, Tuluva dynasty.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The BATTLE OF TALIKOTA (1565), which fatally weakened Vijayanagar, was fought against:
questions.explanation: 26 January 1565 at Talikota (Rakkasa-Tangadi). Four Deccan Sultanates (without Berar) united against Vijayanagar. Ramaraya (regent for Sadashiva Raya) was killed; Hampi was sacked. Empire survived on in a diminished form under the Aravidu dynasty until 1646. Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar.
questions.subject: History

_fixes.was: A confederacy of Deccan Sultanates (Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar)

questions.stem: The foreign traveller whose 'A FORGOTTEN EMPIRE' brought Vijayanagar to global attention was:
questions.explanation: Robert Sewell (British civil servant) wrote 'A Forgotten Empire' (1900) synthesizing accounts by foreign visitors: Abdur Razzak (Persian, 1443), Nicolo Conti (Italian, 1420), Domingo Paes & Fernao Nuniz (Portuguese, early 16th century). Ibn Battuta was 14th-century, pre-Vijayanagar.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Match the VIJAYANAGAR DYNASTY with its FOUNDER. A. Sangama.  B. Saluva.  C. Tuluva.  D. Aravidu. List-II: 1. Harihara I.  2. Saluva Narasimha.  3. Vira Narasimha / Viranarasimha.  4. Tirumala.
questions.explanation: 4 dynasties: Sangama (1336-1485, Harihara I + Bukka I onwards); Saluva (1485-1505, Saluva Narasimha); Tuluva (1505-1565, includes Krishnadeva Raya); Aravidu (1570-1646, Tirumala onwards; from Penukonda / Chandragiri after Talikota).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The RUINS of Vijayanagar are found at:
questions.explanation: Hampi — ruins of Vijayanagar capital in Bellary district, Karnataka. UNESCO WHS 1986. Virupaksha Temple, Vithala Temple (with stone chariot), Hazara Rama Temple, royal enclosures. Halebidu was Hoysala capital. Penukonda became Aravidu capital after 1565.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The PORTUGUESE arrived on India's west coast during the Vijayanagar period. The first Portuguese to land at Calicut was:
questions.explanation: Vasco da Gama — 20 May 1498 at Kappad, near Calicut (Kozhikode). Received by Zamorin. Opened sea route to India; marks start of European colonial era in Asia. Albuquerque captured Goa 1510. Dias reached only as far as Cape of Good Hope. Cabral reached Brazil before coming to India (1500).
